critical_steps: Identity coordinate operators give a Parseval outer weave while local vectors of size 1/n produce the non-frame family e_n/n.
Coordinate operators scaled by 1/n fail the outer lower frame bound while local vectors of size n produce the Parseval family e_n.
Uniform local bounds a and b yield a E_g <= E_vec <= b E_g for every weave.
Those inequalities transfer outer bounds C,D to aC,bD and induced bounds C,D to C/b,D/a.
The published proof itself invokes a global infimum and supremum not guaranteed by its hypotheses.
integrity.proof_basis: Two exact diagonal counterexamples on l2 with one-dimensional coefficient spaces, plus direct comparison of local and outer frame energies.
integrity.unproved_limits: No classification is claimed for specially correlated nonuniform local systems where the equivalence may remain true.

scientific_limitations: The correction concerns the equivalence theorem relating outer continuous g-weaving to weaving of locally induced vectors.

Uniform lower and upper local frame bounds are a clean sufficient repair and are separately necessary for a theorem covering arbitrary local-frame fields; special nonuniform systems can still satisfy the equivalence by compensation.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: Uniform local conditioning is necessary for a continuous \(g\)-weaving equivalence
